outcome: Still open for connected graphs as of October 2026: no event since 26 January 2024 proves the O(√n) bound or improves the general n-vertex bound. The in-window results are restricted-class, parameter, hypergraph or variant results plus one withdrawal, and no mathematics credited to an AI system was found.
problem_asks: (1) For every connected graph G on n vertices, the cop number c(G) is O(√n): there is an absolute constant C with c(G) ≤ C√n for all connected G and all n. The frozen Wikipedia bullet reads 'cop number is O(√n)' without saying connected; the literature (Meyniel, Baird–Bonato, Bose et al. 2026) states it for connected graphs, and I take that reading. (2) The constant C is uniform over all n and all connected graphs. The statement asks for the order √n, not for tightness; lower-bound families of order √n are known (Hasiri–Shinkar; Bonato–Cushman–Marbach; Hosseini et al.), so the content is the upper bound. Not asked by the bullet: the weak form c(G) = O(n^(1−ε)), restrictions to random, bounded-degree, dense, diameter-2 or Cayley-type graphs, and the hypergraph and multi-layer analogues. Each of these is a known partial route and is recorded below as a different question.

events.what_happened: Frankl gave the general upper bound O(n log log n / log n) on cop number for connected graphs, and the conjecture first appears in his paper as a 1985 personal communication from Henri Meyniel. The primary paper was not opened; the bound and the attribution come from the Wikipedia 'Cop number' article (opened), which cites Frankl 1987.
events.delivers: A sublinear general bound, O(n log log n / log n), for connected graphs as reported by secondary sources. Not of order √n and not a restricted case; it is background to the conjecture.
events.remains: The O(√n) claim in full.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture only in the trivial sense that the bound is sublinear. Does not bear on the √n order.

events.what_happened: Linyuan Lu and Xing Peng, 'On Meyniel's conjecture of the cop number', cited as J. Graph Theory 71(2):192–205 (2012). As described by later citing texts (the Bose et al. 2026 abstract and a 2026 search summary), it proves (a) the general bound n/2^((1−o(1))√log n), obtained independently by Scott and Sudakov, and (b) for graphs of diameter 2 and bipartite graphs of diameter 3, c(G) ≤ 2√n − 1 by a random argument, described by later citers as a special case of Meyniel's conjecture. The author PDF returned unreadable binary, so the content of (a) and (b) is from citing texts, not from the paper itself.
events.revisions: Earliest dated evidence: Frieze, Krivelevich and Loh (arXiv 14 Apr 2010) already call the Lu–Peng bound the best known for the classical game, so a preprint existed by April 2010. Later citers give 2011. The journal version is 2012. The preprint itself was not located, so the year is the earliest evidence, not a confirmed first posting.
events.delivers: (a) A general n-vertex bound n/2^((1−o(1))√log n): not of order √n. (b) Per citing texts, for connected graphs of diameter 2 and bipartite graphs of diameter 3, c(G) ≤ 2√n − 1: this is the O(√n) claim for those two classes, a restricted case and not the general conjecture.
events.remains: For (b): every connected graph outside diameter 2 and bipartite diameter 3. For (a): the O(√n) claim for all connected graphs.

checked_by.who: Journal of Graph Theory editors and referees
checked_by.what_they_did: Published vol. 71(2), pp. 192–205 (2012), per citing references; not verified on the journal site

checked_by.qualification: Author of a 2013 cop-number preprint; affiliation not checked
checked_by.what_they_did: Worked through the diameter-2 bound and improved its constant to √(2n), stating that this improves Lu and Peng by a constant factor

events.time_since_posted: about 14 years since the 2012 publication; the 2026 citing texts still call the general bound the best known
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on the two stated diameter classes. The general bound (a) is far from √n, with a saving of 2^(−(1+o(1))√log n) over n.

events.what_happened: Alex Scott and Benny Sudakov, 'A new bound for the cops and robbers problem', arXiv:1004.2010, one version posted 12 April 2010. The abstract proves c(G) ≤ n·2^(−(1+o(1))√log n) for every n-vertex graph and states Meyniel's conjecture (O(√n) for connected graphs) as open. Journal not verified; later citers give 2011.
events.delivers: A general bound for every n-vertex graph, not restricted to connected graphs: c ≤ n·2^(−(1+o(1))√log n). Not of order √n.
events.remains: The O(√n) claim for all connected graphs.
events.time_since_posted: about 16.5 years; later texts cite it as the best known bound
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture as a sublinear general bound; not decisive for √n.

events.what_happened: Alan Frieze, Michael Krivelevich and Po-Shen Loh, 'Variations on Cops and Robbers', arXiv:1004.2482, posted 14 April 2010 (one version); published in J. Graph Theory in 2012 per a search summary (not verified). The robber moves R > 1 edges per turn. The general bound is N/α^((1−o(1))√log_α N) with α = 1 + 1/R, which generalises the Lu–Peng bound for R = 1, and the paper gives an expansion-based second proof of the Lu–Peng bound.
events.delivers: A bound for the faster-robber variant (R > 1). It is not the classical game. Its R = 1 case is the Lu–Peng general bound already recorded. Connectivity is not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: Everything in the classical game.
events.direction: Neighbouring problem (robber faster than cops). Not Meyniel's quantity; its classical special case is the known Lu–Peng bound.

events.what_happened: Abbas Mehrabian, 'Lower Bounds for the Cop Number When the Robber is Fast', arXiv:1007.1734 (first posted 10 July 2010; v2 10 May 2011). With the robber moving t edges per turn, connected n-vertex graphs with cop number Ω(n^(2/3)) for t > 1 and Ω(n^(4/5)) for t > 3. The author conjectures a general upper bound O(n^(t/(t+1))), which the abstract describes as generalising Meyniel's conjecture.
events.delivers: Lower bounds for a faster-robber variant. Does not touch the classical upper bound.
events.remains: The classical problem in full.
events.direction: Neighbouring variant. The conjectured exponent t/(t+1) equals 1/2 at t = 1, which is the link the author draws to the classical √n.
events.object: For the speed-t variant: d-regular graphs of girth above 2t+2 with cop number Ω(d^t), and connected n-vertex graphs with cop number Ω(n^(2/3)) (t > 1) or Ω(n^(4/5)) (t > 3). Explicit construction not read; the abstract gives only the orders.

events.what_happened: Noga Alon and Abbas Mehrabian, 'On a Generalization of Meyniel's Conjecture on the Cops and Robbers Game', Electronic J. Combin. 18(1), #P19, published 19 January 2011. With the robber moving s edges per turn, connected n-vertex graphs with cop number Ω(n^(s/(s+1))), improving Frieze et al.'s Ω(n^((s−3)/(s−2))). The arXiv posting was not located, so the date is the journal year.
events.revisions: None found. arXiv posting not located.
events.delivers: Lower bounds for a faster-robber variant. Does not touch the classical upper bound.
events.remains: The classical problem in full.

checked_by.who: Electronic Journal of Combinatorics editors and referees

events.direction: Neighbouring variant; lower-bound constructions that do not address the classical upper bound.

events.what_happened: Paweł Prałat and Nicholas Wormald, 'Meyniel's conjecture holds for random graphs', arXiv:1301.2841 (first posted 14 January 2013; v2 11 December 2014). Proves Meyniel's conjecture holds asymptotically almost surely for the binomial random graph G(n,p), via a deterministic result for graphs with expansion-type properties. Cited as Random Structures & Algorithms 48(2):396–421 (2016); journal page not opened. One 2026 citing text describes the range of p as above the connectivity threshold; the abstract read does not state the range.
events.delivers: Meyniel's bound for G(n,p), a.a.s. This is a restricted random-graph model. The quantifier 'every connected graph' is not met.
events.remains: Every connected graph outside the random model.

checked_by.who: Random Structures & Algorithms editors and referees
checked_by.what_they_did: Published 48(2), 2016, per citing references; not verified on the journal site
checked_by.where: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.2841 (preprint read; journal page not opened)

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on a restricted random model.

events.what_happened: William Baird and Anthony Bonato, 'Meyniel's conjecture on the cop number: a survey', arXiv:1308.3385 (posted 15 August 2013; one version). Surveys origins and progress, calls the conjecture one of the deepest open problems on the cop number, notes it was largely ignored for over 20 years, and presents new constructions of Meyniel extremal families (cop number at least d√n). Journal venue not stated on the page read.
events.delivers: No resolution. Background, and lower-bound constructions showing the √n order cannot be improved if the conjecture holds.
events.remains: All of the conjecture.
events.direction: Consistent. Its constructions show the √n order is tight if the conjecture holds, and it states the conjecture open.
events.object: Meyniel extremal families: connected graphs with cop number at least d√n, constructed in the survey. The construction details were not read.

events.what_happened: Zsolt Adam Wagner, 'Cops and Robbers on diameter two graphs', arXiv:1312.7555 (first posted 29 December 2013; v3 28 September 2014). Proves the cop number of any diameter-2 graph on n vertices is at most √(2n), improving Lu and Peng's bound by a constant factor, and conjectures this is not optimal, with partial results.
events.delivers: The O(√n) claim for diameter-2 graphs, with c ≤ √(2n). Diameter-2 graphs are connected, so this is a restricted class of connected graphs. It does not reach diameter 3 and above.
events.remains: All connected graphs of diameter at least 3.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on the diameter-2 class.

events.what_happened: Paweł Prałat and Nicholas Wormald, 'Meyniel's conjecture holds for random d-regular graphs', arXiv:1510.03003 (first posted 11 October 2015; v2 22 September 2018). Proves the conjecture holds asymptotically almost surely for random d-regular graphs with d = d(n) ≥ 3, using the deterministic expansion result of the 2013 paper. Cited as Random Structures & Algorithms 55(3):719–741 (2019); not verified.
events.delivers: Meyniel's bound for random d-regular graphs, a.a.s. Restricted model; not all connected graphs.
events.remains: Every connected graph outside the random regular model.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on a restricted random model.

events.what_happened: Anthony Bonato, Jane Breen, Boris Brimkov, Joshua Carlson, Sean English, Jesse Geneson, Leslie Hogben, K.E. Perry and Carolyn Reinhart, 'Optimizing the trade-off between number of cops and capture time in Cops and Robbers', arXiv:1903.10087 (first posted 25 March 2019; v2 13 September 2019). Constructs graphs with cop throttling number Ω(n^(2/3)), gives a sublinear upper bound on throttling, and shows throttling is O(√n) for chordal graphs. The throttling conjecture of Breen et al. (2018), that throttling is O(√n), is the target of the family.
events.delivers: A neighbouring parameter, cop throttling (cops plus capture time), not the cop number. The Ω(n^(2/3)) family refutes a √n bound for throttling. It does not decide the cop-number conjecture. A search summary says the authors note this blocks proving Meyniel via throttling; that sentence was not seen in the abstract read.
events.remains: All of the cop-number conjecture.
events.direction: Neighbouring parameter. Its refutation of a throttling √n bound does not bear on whether the cop number is O(√n).
events.object: A family of graphs with cop throttling number Ω(n^(2/3)). The construction was not read.

events.what_happened: Fatemeh Hasiri and Igor Shinkar, 'Meyniel Extremal Families of Abelian Cayley Graphs', arXiv:1909.03027 (first posted 6 September 2019; one version). Gives several families of abelian Cayley graphs that are Meyniel extremal (cop number Ω(√n)), so the conjectured bound is tight up to a constant for these; also K_{2,3}-free Cayley graphs with Ω(√n) generators. Cited as Graphs and Combinatorics 38(3):61 (2022) per DBLP (DBLP not opened). The same paper cites an O(√n) upper bound for Cayley graphs due to Bradshaw; that citation was not located.
events.delivers: Tightness families only: the √n order cannot be improved for these abelian Cayley graphs if the conjecture holds. No upper bound, and it does not settle the conjecture.
events.remains: All of the conjecture, including the upper bound.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, as lower-bound (tightness) families.
events.object: Abelian Cayley graphs on n vertices with cop number Ω(√n), giving explicit families; K_{2,3}-free Cayley graphs with Ω(√n) generators. Construction details not read.

events.what_happened: Seyyed Aliasghar Hosseini, Bojan Mohar and Sebastian Gonzalez Hermosillo de la Maza, 'Meyniel's conjecture on graphs of bounded degree', arXiv:1912.06957 (submitted 15 December 2019; v2 21 November 2020). Constructs arbitrarily large subcubic graphs with cop number at least n^(1/2−o(1)), so √n is nearly tight for bounded degree. Shows that Meyniel's conjecture for bounded-degree graphs would imply the weak conjecture for all graphs. No journal listed on the page.
events.delivers: A lower bound of order n^(1/2−o(1)) for subcubic graphs, and a conditional reduction. Neither is an upper bound, so the conjecture is not settled.
events.remains: All of the conjecture.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: a near-√n lower bound for bounded degree, plus the reduction.
events.object: Arbitrarily large subcubic graphs with cop number at least n^(1/2−o(1)). The abstract does not say whether the construction is explicit. The construction was not read.
people: Sebastian Gonzalez Hermosillo de la Maza

events.what_happened: Peter Bradshaw, Seyyed Aliasghar Hosseini, Bojan Mohar and Ladislav Stacho, 'On the cop number of graphs of high girth', arXiv:2005.10849 (submitted 21 May 2020). Published as J. Graph Theory 102(1):15–34 on 28 June 2022 (OpenAlex record). Proves a lower bound for high-girth graphs in terms of minimum degree. The abstract states the weak Meyniel conjecture holds for expander graph families of bounded degree.
events.revisions: None found on the arXiv abstract page. Journal version 28 Jun 2022.
events.delivers: The weak form (cop number O(n^(1−α))) for bounded-degree expander families only. Not O(√n), and not all graphs. Also a high-girth lower bound on a different question.
events.remains: The O(√n) bound for those families and for all connected graphs.

checked_by.who: Journal of Graph Theory editors and referees
checked_by.what_they_did: Published vol. 102(1), pp. 15–34, 28 Jun 2022 (OpenAlex record read)

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, in its weak form on a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Anthony Bonato, Ryan Cushman and Trent G. Marbach, 'On Meyniel extremal families of graphs', arXiv:2201.08719 (submitted 21 January 2022; one version). New constructions: exponentially many Meyniel extremal families with prescribed degrees, built from spanning subgraphs; the best known upper bound on cop number of vertex-transitive graphs with a prescribed degree; new regular Meyniel extremal families with large chromatic number and diameter. A search summary says it appeared as 'New constructions of Meyniel extremal families of graphs', Contributions to Discrete Mathematics 21(1) (2026); not verified.
events.delivers: Lower-bound constructions of extremal families, plus a class-restricted upper bound for vertex-transitive graphs of prescribed degree. Does not establish O(√n) for all connected graphs.
events.remains: The upper bound for all connected graphs.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, as tightness families and a vertex-transitive upper bound.
events.object: Exponentially many explicit Meyniel extremal families (cop number of order √n) with prescribed degrees, built from spanning subgraphs. Details not read.

events.what_happened: Jessica Enright, Kitty Meeks, William Pettersson and John Sylvester, 'Cops and Robbers on Multi-Layer Graphs', arXiv:2303.03962 (first posted 7 March 2023; v2 24 November 2023). A multi-layer game in which each cop is confined to one layer and the robber moves in any layer. Shows NP-hardness and that the multi-layer cop number is not controlled by the single-layer cop numbers. Considers a multi-layer variant of Meyniel's conjecture and gives an infinite family with multi-layer cop number at least a constant times n/log n. Journal version: Discrete Applied Mathematics 385 (2026), 109–133, per search summary (not verified).
events.delivers: A different game (multi-layer). Its family refutes the multi-layer analogue of the √n bound. It says nothing about ordinary connected graphs.
events.remains: The ordinary conjecture in full.
events.direction: Counter to the multi-layer analogue only, as the abstract states it. Not a counter to the ordinary conjecture.
events.object: An infinite family of multi-layer graphs whose multi-layer cop number is at least a constant times n/log n. Construction not read.

events.what_happened: Arindam Biswas and Jyoti Prakash Saha, 'On the cop number and the weak Meyniel conjecture for algebraic graphs', arXiv:2303.05381 (v1 9 March 2023; v2 28 April 2025), European Journal of Combinatorics 128, art. 104168 (August 2025). Full text read. Theorem 6.1 (restated as Theorem 1.4): for any undirected connected Cayley graph, Cayley sum graph, twisted Cayley graph or twisted Cayley sum graph of a finite group of order n, the cop number is at most 2√n log n. Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 give at most 2|S| for the twisted cases. The authors deduce O(n^(1−c)) for every c < 1/2 and state the weak Meyniel conjecture for these families.
events.revisions: v2 28 Apr 2025 (v1 content not compared with v2). Journal: European Journal of Combinatorics, Aug 2025.
events.delivers: For undirected connected Cayley-type graphs of a finite group of order n (with the symmetry and conjugation conditions in Theorem 6.1): cop number at most 2√n log n. That is O(√n) up to a log factor, for those families only. The weak form is established for these families. Not all connected graphs.
events.remains: The exact √n order for these families (the bound carries a log factor), and every other connected graph.

checked_by.who: European Journal of Combinatorics editors and referees
checked_by.what_they_did: Published vol. 128, art. 104168 (Aug 2025), per a research-portal listing (not opened)

events.doubts: Restricted to Cayley-type graphs of finite groups. The theorem's hypotheses (symmetry, conjugation closure, order-two automorphism) narrow the class further.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on Cayley-type families, where the bound is within a log factor of √n.

events.what_happened: Alexander Clow, 'Graphs with Large Girth and Small Cop Number', arXiv:2306.00220. Versions: v1 31 May 2023; v2 2 June 2023; v3 6 June 2023; v4 19 July 2024 (current). Current abstract: for girth g and minimum degree δ with δ ≥ n^(2/g+ε), c(G) = O(√n), which is Meyniel's bound for those graphs; for δ ≥ n^ε and girth g ≥ 7, c(G) = O(n^(1−α)) for some α > 0 (the weak form). The full v4 text was read: no AI disclosure, NSERC acknowledgement only. The v1–v3 abstracts were not read.
events.revisions: v2 2 Jun 2023; v3 6 Jun 2023; v4 19 Jul 2024 (in the window). Scope of v1–v3 not compared with v4.
events.delivers: The O(√n) bound for connected graphs with minimum degree at least n^(2/g+ε), where g is the girth; and the weak bound for girth at least 7 and minimum degree at least n^ε. Restricted to dense or high-girth graphs. Sparse graphs and the general conjecture remain.
events.remains: Graphs with minimum degree below n^(2/g+ε), including sparse and bounded-degree graphs, and the conjecture in full.
events.time_since_posted: about 3.4 years from v1; about 2.2 years from v4
events.doubts: Restricted class. The v4 abstract has an apparent typo ('there δ≥nε') in the weak statement, read as δ ≥ n^ε. No journal publication was found in the searches. The PR #10 catalogue cites this paper, which is not a mathematical engagement.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Alexander Clow, 'Expanders Satisfy the Weak Meyniel Conjecture', arXiv:2311.13792. v1 posted 23 November 2023; v2 27 November 2023; v3 9 February 2024, withdrawn. The abstract read (withdrawn page) states that for sequences of graphs with bounded maximum degree and isoperimetric constant bounded away from 0, the cop number is O(n^((1+α)/2+o(1))), which is sublinear and is a weak-form result for bounded-degree expanders. The paper says counterexamples to the weak conjecture would have to be expanders. The arXiv page comment says its results are captured by Theorem 4.3 of the journal article doi 10.1002/jgt.22855, which is the Bradshaw et al. paper.
events.delivers: As read on the withdrawn page: a sublinear bound for bounded-degree expander families. It is a restricted class, and it is withdrawn. The page says its content is captured by a 2022 journal theorem.
events.remains: The O(√n) claim and the weak conjecture for all graphs.
events.doubts: Withdrawn in v3. The withdrawal page gives no reason beyond the comment that the results are captured by Theorem 4.3 of doi 10.1002/jgt.22855. The v1–v2 text was not read.

withdrawn.what: The preprint was withdrawn in v3. Its v1–v2 claim was a sublinear bound, O(n^((1+α)/2+o(1))), for bounded-degree expanders.
withdrawn.by: Not stated on the arXiv abstract page read; the withdrawal is an arXiv v3 status

events.direction: Restricted class, withdrawn. Its stated result is captured by an earlier journal theorem, per the page comment.

events.what_happened: Quentin Deschamps, Carl Feghali, František Kardoš, Clément Legrand-Duchesne and Théo Pierron, 'Strengthening a Theorem of Meyniel', SIAM J. Discrete Math. 37(2):604–611, published 17 May 2023 (OpenAlex record). It concerns the diameter of the Kempe-change reconfiguration graph of k-colourings of planar graphs, strengthening a 1978 Meyniel theorem. The arXiv posting was not checked.
events.revisions: None checked. The arXiv posting date was not located; the journal date is 17 May 2023.
events.delivers: Nothing on the cop-number conjecture. It is a name-sharing result (Meyniel 1978, Kempe changes), so it is a different question.
events.remains: All of the cop-number conjecture.
events.direction: Different problem: a namesake result about colourings, not cops and robbers.

events.what_happened: Joshua Erde, Mihyun Kang, Florian Lehner, Bojan Mohar and Dominik Schmid, 'Catching a robber on a random k-uniform hypergraph', arXiv:2307.15512 (first posted 28 July 2023; v2 11 April 2024). Shows with high probability the cop number of the random k-uniform hypergraph G^k(n,p) is O(√(n/k) log n) over a broad range of p and k. Conjectures that connected k-uniform hypergraphs on n vertices have cop number O(√(n/k)). The paper cites Meyniel's graph conjecture as background. At k = 2 the hypergraph conjecture is the graph conjecture.
events.delivers: A random-hypergraph bound with a log factor, and a conjecture for hypergraphs. It is not a graph result and does not settle Meyniel's conjecture.
events.remains: The graph conjecture (k = 2), which is the special case of the stated hypergraph conjecture.
events.direction: A hypergraph analogue that contains the graph conjecture at k = 2. It is a generalisation, not partial progress on the graph case.

events.what_happened: Suryaansh Jain, Subrahmanyam Kalyanasundaram and Kartheek Sriram Tammana, 'A bound for the cops and robber problem in terms of 2-component order connectivity', arXiv:2412.02511 (submitted 3 December 2024; 5 pages). Bounds the cop number of a graph in terms of its 2-component order connectivity. The abstract read does not give the formula and does not mention Meyniel's conjecture.
events.delivers: A cop-number bound in a graph parameter (2-component order connectivity), not in n. It does not move the general n-bound unless it beats n/2^((1−o(1))√log n) for general graphs, which was not established because the formula was not read.
events.remains: The O(√n) claim for connected graphs in terms of n.
events.direction: Parameter-based bound. No bearing on the √n claim unless it yields a better n-bound, which was not established.

events.what_happened: Prosenjit Bose, Pat Morin and Karthik Murali, 'Cops and Robbers for Graphs on Surfaces with Crossings', arXiv:2504.13813 (submitted 18 April 2025; v2 2 July 2025), an MFCS 2025 extended abstract. Studies distance-d cops and robbers, in which the robber is captured when a cop is within distance d. Shows bounded cop number for graphs whose crossing pairs of edges are joined by short paths. The abstract does not mention Meyniel's conjecture.
events.delivers: A different game (distance-d capture) on graphs with crossings. It does not bear on the classical cop number or on the √n order.
events.remains: All of the conjecture.
events.direction: Different question: a different capture rule on a different class.

events.what_happened: Zhaoyu Wu, '4K1 free graphs on 13 vertices have cop number at most 2', arXiv:2601.00917 (v1 1 January 2026; v2 14 January 2026). The abstract claims that for any G in Forb(4K1) (independence number below 4), c(G) ≤ 2. It improves a lower bound for a question of Char et al. and concerns Turcotte's conjecture for p = 4. The title restricts the result to 13 vertices, which the abstract's 'any G' wording does not. Meyniel's conjecture and the O(√n) bound are not mentioned.
events.delivers: Cop number at most 2 for a graph class (independence number below 4), on the stated scope. It concerns Turcotte's question and not the √n claim.
events.remains: All of the conjecture.
events.doubts: The title (13 vertices) and the abstract ('for any G') disagree on scope. The full text was not read.
events.direction: Neighbouring problem (Turcotte's question on 4K1-free graphs). Not Meyniel's quantity.

events.what_happened: Prosenjit Bose, Louis Esperet, Jędrzej Hodor, Gwenaël Joret, Piotr Micek and Clément Rambaud, 'Cops and robber in graphs with bounded vertex cover number', arXiv:2602.07435 (submitted 7 February 2026; one version; math.CO, cross-listed cs.DM). States Meyniel's conjecture as open. Proves a connected graph with vertex cover number k has cop number at most k/2^((1−o(1))√log k), the first sublinear bound in vertex cover number, and restates the best general bound n/2^((1−o(1))√log n) of Lu–Peng and Scott–Sudakov. Full text read: no AI or LLM disclosure, no contribution statement; funding footnotes and a Bellairs workshop acknowledgement (research initiated February 2025).
events.delivers: A bound in the vertex cover number k, not in n. Since k ≤ n, it does not improve the general bound in n and gives no O(√n) bound for general connected graphs. Its k/2^((1−o(1))√log k) is the new content.
events.remains: Every connected graph whose vertex cover number is not small, and the O(√n) claim in n for all connected graphs.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture (sublinear, parameterised). No counter-result.

The PR claims no new mathematics.

events.what_happened: Gabriel Dias (listed in the arXiv submission history as Gabriel Dias Do Couto), 'On Meyniel's Conjecture in Random Hypergraphs', arXiv:2606.27066 (submitted 25 June 2026; one version; math.CO). Proves the Erde et al. hypergraph conjecture (cop number O(√(n/k))) for a class of expanding k-uniform hypergraphs with k ≥ log³ n, and shows with high probability for random k-uniform hypergraphs H^k(n,p) under k ≥ log³ n and degree conditions. Full text read: no AI disclosure; the paper states the graph conjecture remains far off. Section 6 says the approach 'could work all the way down to k=2 (the graph case)' only with further work.
events.delivers: A hypergraph generalisation for expanding k-uniform hypergraphs with k ≥ log³ n, and for random hypergraphs under the same restriction. It does not cover k = 2, so it does not prove the graph conjecture.
events.remains: Ordinary connected graphs (k = 2), and hypergraphs with k below log³ n.
events.direction: Consistent with the hypergraph analogue; the theorems exclude the graph case.

disputes.summary: The general bound n/2^((1−o(1))√log n) is credited 'independently' to Lu and Peng and to Scott and Sudakov, and 2026 citers date both to 2011. Scott and Sudakov's arXiv preprint is dated 12 April 2010, and Frieze, Krivelevich and Loh (arXiv 14 April 2010) already call the Lu–Peng bound the best known for the classical game. So Lu–Peng existed in preprint form by April 2010. Which result came first is not settled here, because the Lu–Peng preprint was not located.

summary: I ran 43 searches and opened about 40 sources, including full texts of the in-window papers. Meyniel's conjecture (cop number O(√n) for connected n-vertex graphs) is still open in every source read. The most recent sources are Dias (25 Jun 2026) and Bose et al. (7 Feb 2026), and the Wikipedia 'Cop number' article as last edited 5 Feb 2026 says proving or disproving the conjecture remains unsolved. Since 26 January 2024 nothing has moved the general bound n/2^((1−o(1))√log n), and nothing settles the conjecture for all connected graphs. The in-window events are: (i) Clow, arXiv 2306.00220, first posted May 2023 and revised to v4 on 19 July 2024, giving O(√n) for graphs with minimum degree at least n^(2/g+ε) and the weak form for girth at least 7; (ii) Bose et al. (Feb 2026), a bound k/2^((1−o(1))√log k) in the vertex cover number k, which cannot improve the bound in n because k ≤ n; (iii) Dias (Jun 2026), a proof of the Erde et al. hypergraph analogue for expanding k-uniform hypergraphs with k ≥ log³ n and for random hypergraphs, which the paper says does not reach the graph case k = 2; (iv) Clow's 'Expanders Satisfy the Weak Meyniel Conjecture', first posted Nov 2023 and withdrawn on 9 Feb 2024, whose page says its results are captured by Bradshaw et al. (JGT 2022); and (v) a September 2026 catalogue entry giving the conjecture a 'partial, high confidence' label, which the repository README says was generated by Claude (Sonnet 4.6). The catalogue entry is a status label, not mathematics. Restricted-class results predate the window and are what the judging pass has to weigh: Wagner (diameter-2 graphs, c ≤ √(2n), Dec 2013); Lu–Peng (per citing texts, c ≤ 2√n − 1 for diameter-2 and bipartite diameter-3 graphs, 2010–2012); Prałat–Wormald (a.a.s. for G(n,p) in 2013 and for random d-regular graphs in 2015); Bradshaw et al. (weak form for bounded-degree expander families, 2020); and Biswas–Saha (verified in the full text: for undirected connected Cayley-type graphs of a group of order n, c ≤ 2√n log n, which is O(√n) up to a log factor for those families; in-window v2 April 2025, EJC August 2025). None of these is the conjecture for all connected graphs. AI: I searched explicitly for AI results on this conjecture, through AI counterexample news, GPT-5.6 claims on other conjectures, the Erdős AI results, the OpenAI 722-manuscript release (openai/math), AlphaEvolve's 67-problem list, the AI co-mathematician paper, Lean/formal-conjectures, and AI-result trackers. None credits an AI system with work on this conjecture. The only AI involvement found is the catalogue labelling described above, which is not in the mathematics. Full-text AI checks were done for the in-window papers (Bose et al., Dias, Clow v4, Biswas–Saha v2); for the pre-2024 items, only abstracts and metadata were read. Close calls: (a) whether Biswas–Saha's 2√n log n on Cayley-type families is 'O(√n)' for the purposes of the problem, given the log factor and the restriction; (b) whether Clow v4's restricted scope is new in July 2024, since v1–v3 were not read; (c) whether Lu–Peng's diameter-2 bound is a resolution of a class or a special case, since the paper itself was not readable here; (d) whether a Cayley-graph O(√n) bound attributed to Bradshaw (cited in Hasiri–Shinkar) exists, since it was not located. The priority question between Lu–Peng and Scott–Sudakov is recorded in disputes. A name collision, Deschamps et al., 'Strengthening a Theorem of Meyniel' (SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2023), concerns Kempe changes and is not this problem. The Wikipedia list bullet reads 'Meyniel's conjecture that cop number is O(n)' in visible text, with the formula as an image whose alt text is O(√n); the frozen January 2024 wording was not checked directly.
competing_reading: Read the restricted results together and the conjecture looks substantially settled for many classes. Lu–Peng/Wagner (diameter 2), Prałat–Wormald (random graphs), Bradshaw et al. (bounded-degree expanders), Biswas–Saha (Cayley-type families, within a log factor) and Clow's high-minimum-degree results cover a broad set of families, and the catalogue's 'partial' label reads that way. The opposite reading is that each is a special case of a universal claim, and the bullet asks about every connected graph, which none of them reaches. A judge who counts 'a class settled' as a resolution would give a very different answer from one who does not.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The Lu–Peng paper itself (J. Graph Theory 71(2), 2012), to confirm the diameter-2 and bipartite diameter-3 bounds and the first posting date. (2) The Bradshaw O(√n) result for Cayley graphs cited by Hasiri–Shinkar, if it is in print. (3) Clow's v1–v3 of arXiv 2306.00220, to see whether the v4 restrictions were new in July 2024. (4) Any arXiv posting after 13 October 2026 claiming the general O(√n) bound or a counterexample, which this search could not reach beyond indexed results. (5) For the AI question: the 372 family manuscripts in openai/math (only the CONTENTS.md map and the lean/formalization.yaml were read, and only through a summarising reader), the rest of the AlphaEvolve problem list past section 26, the full text of arXiv 2605.06651 and of Sra's 'GPT, the Counterexample Machine' (2608.29595), and the full text of the Bradshaw paper's AI disclosures if any.
